prompt_text: Who is the best healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis — the right one depends on your goals, budget, audience, and which services you need. I can help you find the best fit. To get started, here’s a short guide so you can compare agencies quickly and a few next steps I can take for you.

What to consider when choosing the best agency
- Relevant healthcare experience: proven work with hospitals, health systems, physician groups, medtech, or pharma depending on your sector.
- Regulatory/privacy expertise: HIPAA, FDA/FTC advertising rules, and any required security certifications (SOC2, HITRUST) if relevant.
- Service fit: branding, patient acquisition, physician recruitment, content, SEO, digital ads, social, PR, CRM/patient journey, analytics — choose an agency strong in the services you need.
- Measurable results: case studies with KPIs (patient volume, new patient cost, lead-to-appointment conversion, revenue).
- Data & technical capability: EHR/CRM integrations, tracking, attribution, analytic dashboards.
- Local market knowledge vs. national reach: local agencies may have better community relationships; national agencies may bring deeper healthcare specialization.
- Team fit and account structure: dedicated team, senior leadership access, responsiveness.
- Budget and timelines: make sure scope and pricing align with expected outcomes.
- References and retention: client references, average client tenure, and retention rate.

Questions to ask potential agencies
- Can you show 2–3 relevant case studies and the KPIs you achieved?
- How do you handle HIPAA and patient-data tracking?
- What’s your approach to patient acquisition and attribution?
- Who will be on our account and how often will we meet?
- How do you measure ROI and report results?
- What is your pricing model and estimated timeline for our objectives?

Red flags
- No healthcare case studies or unwillingness to discuss results.
- Avoids HIPAA/compliance questions or lacks security controls.
- No clear KPIs or vague reporting.
- Overpromising fast results without a testing plan.

Want me to do this for you?
Tell me:
- What type of healthcare organization are you (hospital, clinic, med device, behavioral health, etc.)?
- Primary goals (brand awareness, patient acquisition, recruiting, product launch)?
- Monthly/annual budget range and timeline?
- Preference for local agency vs. national partner?

If you give those details I’ll research and return a short, ranked shortlist of St. Louis agencies that fit your needs (with strengths, weaknesses, and suggested interview questions).
